title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
text:
Thank you for your interest in joining my laboratory through the International Graduate Program (IGP).
I welcome inquiries from students whose academic interests are closely related to my research. I particularly welcome inquiries from prospective PhD students, as well as prospective master’s students who are strongly research-oriented and are considering continuing to doctoral studies in the future. Before contacting me, please read the information below carefully.

title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
text:
1. Research fit
Before sending an email, please make sure that your research interests are clearly connected to my current work. I encourage you to read several of my recent papers on the Research page and to explain specifically why you are interested in my research group.

title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
section: 2. What to include in your email
text:
2. What to include in your email
When contacting me for the first time, please include the following information in a single email:

your full name and current affiliation
the degree program you wish to apply for
your academic background and research interests
a brief explanation of why you want to work with me
your CV
your academic transcript
your English test score, if available
a brief research proposal or statement of purpose

Please write your email clearly and concisely.

title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
text:
3. Important note
Please note that contacting me does not guarantee supervision or admission. Any decision depends on the match between your interests and my research, my supervisory capacity, and the official admission process of the university.

title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
text:
4. Official application requirements
The information on this page is only intended as guidance for students who wish to contact me in advance. For official eligibility requirements, application procedures, and deadlines, please make sure to consult the university’s official IGP website:

International Graduate Program — Institute of Science Tokyo

title: For Prospective IGP Applicants
text:
5. Response policy
Because I receive many inquiries, I may not be able to reply to every email. I am more likely to respond to applicants whose research interests closely match my work and whose emails include the materials listed above.

This project develops a theory of credibility as a scarce resource in information markets.

title: Research Projects
text:
Proofs without Disclosure
This project studies strategic communication with privacy-preserving verifiable proofs.

title: Research Projects
text:
Firm Dynamics after IPO
This project examines how financial intermediary heterogeneity affects post-IPO growth, valuation, debt capacity, and upper-tail firm dynamics in Japan.

title: Research Projects
text:
Incremental Value of Data
This project studies the value of data through conditional mutual information and prediction-based decision problems.

title: Research
text: I work at the intersection of corporate finance, information economics, and firm dynamics. My research asks how firms and investors produce, disclose, and act on information under uncertainty — and how those decisions aggregate into market outcomes. Recurring threads include the value of information and data, managerial behavior and cognition, institutional investor engagement, and innovation and corporate networks, studied with both theoretical models and large-scale text and patent data.

Payoff-Relevant Information Architecture

This paper develops a decision-theoretic model of the incremental value of data and shows how conditional mutual information characterizes the value of an additional signal.
